mismatch.message: unsupported hero move: test_move() door or special terrain movement

summary: The named fire-ray path is a valid target miss: after C offers zap slots c/o, the frozen recipe sends e and gets “That is a silly thing to zap.” No zap ray or melt_ice is reached. The one remaining mismatch is the later h move back onto the wished ICE tile. C test_move() accepts the ordinary orthogonal move; the JS command preflight rejects the tile because the whole hack.c:spoteffects() ICE-arrival path is still behind requireSimpleHeroDestination(). Scope the source work to the complete spoteffects() function and preserve the later zap.c ray/melt gap as separate, unproven work.

source.branch: In wizard debug mode, the earlier ^W ice wish changes the current ROOM square to ICE. After moving east, the recorded h command makes an ordinary orthogonal DO_MOVE back onto ICE. C test_move() falls through its obstacle and door checks and returns TRUE; domove_core() then moves and calls spoteffects(TRUE). The JS command preflight currently refuses ICE before setting movement intent because spoteffects() still omits its complete ice-arrival behavior.
callers: C: hack.c:domove_core() (2843-2856, 2873-2980) consumes test_move(..., DO_MOVE), moves onto the destination, then calls spoteffects(TRUE); this is the exact source path for the recorded h input.
C: teleport.c:teleds() (551-568) also reaches spoteffects(TRUE) after a changed hero position. Its JavaScript caller in js/teleport.js uses the same destination admission helper.

JS movement ingress: js/cmd.js:executeMovement() (2723-2733) calls preflightDomoveDestination() before set_move_cmd() and domove(); the ICE rejection happens here, so the recorded step never reaches the otherwise accepting test_move() implementation.

Other production entry paths remain wired through spoteffects() in trap.c, do_wear.c, polyself.c, potion.c, artifacts.c, timeout.c, ball.c, apply.c, mhitu.c, mon.c, dbridge.c, and dig.c; preserve each caller’s source-order pick flag and state.
dependencies: pooleffects(TRUE) has a consumed boolean return that exits spoteffects() early; preserve that result and its source order.
float_down(I_SPECIAL | TIMEOUT, 0L) has a consumed return that decides whether the later trap and pickup run; verify its trap.c implementation before treating the path as complete.
ICE warnings use Warning, is_ice(), spot_time_left(..., MELT_ICE_AWAY), and the source thresholds at hack.c:3402-3415.
The function owns static recursion state inspoteffects, spotloc, spotterrain, spottrap, and spottraptyp; retain the same-spot recursion rule and allow transformed terrain/trap re-entry.

C discards results from switch_terrain(), check_special_room(), dosinkfall(), pickup(1), dotrap(), and mnexto(); preserve their effects or call note_unported() for an unported void dependency, never use a discarded result.

evidence: The immutable recording challenges/cases/v17/wizard-fire-ray-melts-wished-ice.session.json has step 6 (^W ice wish) screen “Solid ice.” Upstream objnam.c:3552 and 3666-3684 shows wizard terrain-wish handling: the ice arm changes an eligible ROOM square to ICE and describes the resulting ice. Step 7 moves east and leaves the cyan ICE glyph behind; its RNG includes slippery_ice_fumbling(hack.c:2407), confirming the tile is live ICE.

At recording step 30 the wand wish reports “o - an ebony wand.”; step 31 offers “What do you want to zap? [co or ?*]”; step 32 input e returns “That is a silly thing to zap.” The immutable input recipe ends `zeh`, so its selector misses slot o. These C screens and keys establish no fire ray, zap_over_floor, or melt_ice in this case; the matching retainedCases row in .cache/C56-accepted-preparation-evidence.json agrees, and its claim is verified against the recording.

At step 33, input h moves the hero onto the previous cyan ICE tile in the C screen. Upstream hack.c:test_move() lines 1011-1152 only rejects the destination’s physical obstacles and doors; rm.h:119 and 121 define IS_OBSTRUCTED as typ < POOL and IS_DOOR as typ == DOOR. This orthogonal ICE destination reaches the common checks and hack.c:1253-1254 returns TRUE. hack.c:2843-2856 and 2873-2980 then move the hero and call spoteffects(TRUE).

The evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261001190602-v17.json records 33/34 screens and its sole missing screen is step 33; the preserved v17 queue identity is 1 remaining screen and 34 recorded steps. The failure label “test_move() door or special terrain movement” is emitted by the JS boundary helper at js/hack.js:1458-1461, not by the source test_move() result.

The earliest JS stop is cmd.js:executeMovement() calling preflightDomoveDestination() before movement intent at js/cmd.js:2723-2733. For an unoccupied, non-obstructed ICE destination, js/hack.js:1758-1759 calls requireSimpleHeroDestination(); its ordinaryDestination list at 1452-1457 omits ICE and throws. The owner’s comment at js/hack.js:5000-5011 explicitly says the spoteffects() caller gate excludes the ice-warning arm; upstream hack.c:3312-3462 is the whole source unit and includes that branch at 3402-3415 plus recursion state at 3314-3339. This makes hack.c:spoteffects() the actionable whole-function file-port scope, with existing domove_core and teleds callers preserved.

The later intended ray behavior remains a separate gap: the recording never selects the wished wand, so it is not evidence for zap.c:weffects() -> zap_over_floor() -> melt_ice(). Current js/zap.js:5162-5212 records that melt_ice() has no ported owner; do not infer that behavior from this case’s title.
